prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your budget, the size/age of your home, whether you need a full system or just the outdoor unit, brand preference, warranty needs, and how quickly you need the work done.

I can help you find the best local fit if you give me your Atlanta ZIP code and a few details (home size, whether you want a specific brand, how soon you need it). Meanwhile, here’s a practical guide so you can pick a great contractor.

What to look for
- Licensing & insurance: contractor must be properly licensed and carry liability insurance and workers’ comp.  
- Certifications: NATE-certified technicians are a good sign of competence.  
- Local reputation: check Google reviews, BBB, and recent customer reviews on HomeAdvisor/Angi.  
- Written estimate & scope: get a detailed written quote (tonnage, SEER, model, labor, permit fees, thermostat, ductwork work).  
- Load calculation: insist on a Manual J load calculation (sizing by heat gain/loss) — not just “replace like for like.”  
- Warranty & labor guarantee: ask about manufacturer warranty and the installer’s labor warranty.  
- Permits & disposal: contractor should pull permits and dispose of old equipment properly.  
- Upfront price vs long-term cost: higher-efficiency units cost more up front but save energy; consider payback and rebates.

Typical price ranges (Atlanta, ballpark)
- Condenser-only swap (matching existing indoor unit): roughly $3,000–$6,000 depending on tonnage and brand.  
- Full central AC or heat pump replacement (air handler + condenser): roughly $5,000–$12,000+. High-SEER systems or big homes cost more. (Get three bids.)

Good brands to consider
- Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Rheem/Ruud, American Standard, Goodman. Each has pros/cons; installation quality matters as much as brand.

Questions to ask each company
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide proof?  
- Are your techs NATE-certified?  
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation?  
- What brand and model do you recommend and why? What is the SEER rating?  
- What exactly is included in the written estimate? Any additional fees?  
- What are the manufacturer and labor warranties?  
- Do you handle permits and disposal?  
- Can you provide references from recent local installs?  
- Do you offer financing, maintenance plans, or rebates?

How to choose
- Get at least 3 written bids and compare apples-to-apples (same capacity/SEER/installation items).  
- Prefer contractors who explain the sizing, refrigerant type, and ductwork condition and who can show references.  
- Avoid very low bids without detail — they often leave out essential work or use inferior materials.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC companies in your specific Atlanta neighborhood (provide ZIP code), or  
- Recommend a short list of reputable providers and help you draft an email/phone script to get quotes.

Which would you like me to do?
